root_cause_label: Agent adopted a false premise at step 6 that fasttext was fully functional on Python 3.13 (because import succeeded) without testing actual predict/inference calls, then misdiagnosed the task as 'fasttext missing from the default Python 3.12 venv' rather than 'NumPy API incompatibility in the system Python 3.13 fasttext installation' — never patching /usr/local/lib/python3.13/site-packages/fasttext/FastText.py
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent mistook a successful import on Python 3.13 as proof of full fasttext compatibility, then spent the entire trajectory installing fasttext into a venv-linked Python 3.12 interpreter instead of applying the required NumPy-compatibility patch to the system Python 3.13 fasttext source.
t_err_evidence: Step 6: agent runs '/usr/local/bin/python3.13 -c "import fasttext; print(...)"' and sees it succeed, concluding fasttext 'works' on Python 3.13. This is a false premise — the task requires fixing a deeper NumPy API incompatibility (np.array copy=False) in the system fasttext that causes failures at predict/inference time, not just at import. The agent never tested actual fasttext usage (e.g., model.predict) and adopted the wrong belief that the only problem was fasttext being absent from the venv Python 3.12.
t_commit_evidence: Step 16: agent bootstraps pip into the venv-linked Python 3.12 interpreter via 'curl -sS https://bootstrap.pypa.io/get-pip.py | python3', committing fully to the wrong remediation path (installing fasttext into the wrong Python env). After this point the agent exclusively works on getting fasttext into the venv Python 3.12 and never revisits patching the system Python 3.13 fasttext.
trigger_explanation: At step 6, the agent tests 'import fasttext' under Python 3.13 and it succeeds, so the agent concludes Python 3.13 fasttext is functional and the only problem is that the default python3 (venv 3.12) lacks fasttext. The agent never verified that fasttext's runtime methods (predict, load_model inference) work under Python 3.13 + NumPy 2.x, which is where the np.array(copy=False) incompatibility manifests. This unverified assumption becomes the foundation of the entire (wrong) remediation strategy.
forewarning_evidence: Step 8: agent tries to install fasttext into /usr/bin/python3 (3.11) which has no pip — command_error signals wrong target environment. Steps 8 and 14 both fail with 'No module named pip' when trying to install for non-target interpreters. These repeated failures signal that the environment is not set up for installation in the way the agent expects, yet the agent does not reconsider the strategy.
